newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH BURY VICTIM OF SOCCER GANG VIOLENCE.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH BURY VICTIM OF SOCCER GANG VIOLENCE.

text.p: An Ajax Amsterdam soccer club gang leader killed last Sunday in a pitched battle with rival supporters was buried on Thursday after a procession from the club's old ground by hundreds of fellow fans.

Carlo Picornie, a 35-year-old hotel owner and leader of Ajax's hard-core "F-side" supporters, was clubbed to death during a bloody clash with Feyenoord Rotterdam fans on waste ground by a motorway near Amsterdam.
Dutch television showed hundreds of Ajax fans gathering at the club's former De Meer stadium in west Amsterdam, before marching under the watchful eye of police to the graveyard for the burial.
Mourners placed hundreds of red and while flowers -- the Ajax club colours -- by the grave.
Bystanders reflected the prevailing mood of sadness and futility over the latest in a series of ugly incidents bedevilling the Dutch game.
"I think it's terrible, but it's got absolutely nothing to do with football," one man said. "It's a disaster, of course, and I just hope they've learnt something from it."
The death was the first linked to the soccer hooliganism that has blighted the sport in this soccer-mad country for over 20 years.
"It is terrible that this can happen to a sport," one elderly woman said, adding that her young son was now too frightened to travel on Amsterdam's metro wearing his favourite Ajax shirt.
The Dutch ANP news agency said police had this week arrested four Feyenoord fans thought to have taken part in Sunday's swift and brutal confrontation. One was later released.

As politicians and the authorities grapple with how to react to the latest soccer violence, especially as the Netherlands is to co-host the European soccer championships in 2000, one "F-side" member told Dutch television: "We cannot and will not forgive".
